narrative.overview:
Earth's Pulse reads as an oceanographic instrument bay, not a dashboard for selling one. The system borrows its composure from research charts and observatory consoles: a near-black navy field, one dominant computed field plate, hairline rules, and monospaced annotations that behave like measured labels. The page is quiet enough that the ocean field can carry it, and exact enough that provenance can interrupt the mood without feeling bolted on.

Everything is rectangular and flat. Depth comes from tone rather than stacked shadows, and the only ambient lift belongs to the field plate. Status is always spelled out next to its color. The layout gives the field the first viewport and keeps the reading and evidence in a permanent rail, so the visual, the sound, and the numbers are read together.

Stage 2 adds a second channel without changing the visual language: the plate is computed from the bundled Int16 field, the transport is live, and the rail reads the same sample that is sounding. Motion remains functional: advected particles show current direction, the playhead shows position, and the transport only changes on state. There is no entrance choreography, no equalizer decoration, and no fake audio meter.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black navy fields with blue-grey hairlines.
One rectangular 2:1 computed field plate as the dominant object.
Inter for reading; IBM Plex Mono only for identifiers, coordinates, timestamps, and measurements.
Cyan for available, running, or focused; neutral grey for ready or paused; amber for a genuine error or missing condition.
Flat panels, square corners, and one deep plate shadow.
Missing data shown as text and silence, never as a zero value.
A visible nonvisual path: reading panel, speech, live region, and full table.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Cyan means available, running, or focused; amber means blocked, failed, or missing. Neutral grey means ready or paused. Never use one of these hues for decoration.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with 1px rules and tonal shifts, not with rounded cards, glass, or shadows on panels.

rules.name: The Honest Silence Rule
rules.body: A missing value silences its voice. It is never mapped to zero, to the coldest temperature, or to slack water.

rules.name: The Measurement Mono Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono is reserved for identifiers, coordinates, timestamps, units, machine status, audio values, and compact data values. Prose stays in Inter.

rules.name: The Quiet Heading Rule
rules.body: Headings gain emphasis through size and weight, never through gradient fills, shadows, or all-caps display type.

rules.name: The Reading Size Rule
rules.body: The values that drive the sound never drop below 16px, even at 390px.

rules.name: The Single Lift Rule
rules.body: Only the field plate casts a shadow. Header, rail panels, transport, tables, and callouts stay flat on their tonal layer.

dos: Do keep the computed field plate as the largest, first-read object on Explore.
Do use 1px hairlines and tonal surfaces to separate regions before reaching for any shadow.
Do pair every status color with a text label and a nearby reason.
Do reserve IBM Plex Mono for identifiers, coordinates, timestamps, units, measurements, and machine status.
Do keep reading measure between 61ch and 68ch and preserve the 2:1 plate ratio.
Do make silence mean missing data, and say Missing in the reading.
Do name the depth of each product: currents at 15 m, temperature at 0 m.
Do keep the page background at Abyss and the plate frame on Deep Panel so the field remains the brightest surface.
donts: Don't introduce gradients, glassmorphism, neon glows, or decorative blur.
Don't wrap panels in rounded cards or add shadows to rail panels, the header, or the transport.
Don't communicate availability with color alone.
Don't sample rendered pixel colors as measurements or imply that the NASA plate is numerical data.
Don't map a missing value to zero, to the coldest temperature, or to slack water.
Don't call the data live, current, or a forecast.
Don't describe particle displacement as real-time or to scale.
Don't use marketing hero metrics, card grids, oversized slogans, or chart-like ornament that implies data we do not have.
Don't make a disabled control look active or hide the reason it cannot be used.
Don't use the mono face for prose.
